output.brief: The rejections came from our own paperwork, not from the fungicide, Lower Serra growers, or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation system, the mandarin product record was copied from avocados on 1 Aug. It carried a 7.0°C carriage temperature instead of our 4.0°C specification. Every Meridane container since then was sent at 7.0°C, and the controller downloads show the units held that setpoint. All five of those containers were rejected, with 9–14% decay. All four containers sent at 4.0°C passed, including Coastway and Pellacor-treated lots (K5, K7). The fungicide is not the cause, because K5 and K7 used Pellacor and passed. Meridane did what it was told. Lower Serra fruit decayed more within the rejected containers, but that is not shown to be the cause, since fruit from other districts also decayed above tolerance. I'm very confident in this diagnosis. Next steps: correct the product record to 4.0°C now. Have Meridane reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check comparing booking temperature with the product specification. Don't suspend Lower Serra, don't claim against Meridane, and don't revert the fungicide. Loggers in containers are a reasonable extra safeguard.
